Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

national anthem noun

also anthem

classical

Curt. 3.3.9

carmen patrium

noun phrase: carmen, carminis n., with the adjective patrium

a national song; the national anthem

Curtius’s phrase, which Lewis & Short render “a national song”: the hymn the Persian Magi sang at the head of the king’s procession. Patrius here is “of one’s own country”, as in patrius sermō, one’s mother tongue (Cic. Fin. 1.4, Lewis & Short). Traupman, Morgan–Owens and Levi–Bini have no word for an anthem; using the phrase for one is our choice.

Examples

  • Magī proximī patrium carmen canēbant

    next came the Magi, singing their national hymnCurt. 3.3.9

  • Carmen patrium canitur; surgāmus.

    They’re playing the national anthem; let’s stand up.composed

See also flag, song, hymn, state.

SourcesLewis & Short: carmen · Lewis & Short: patrius
